Same as on our LS Lexus. If the battery gets below a safe charge state it will shut off the HID lighting and drop you to the back up old fashioned head lights. Used the OBD menu and found that the throttle body sensors were not in agreement due to a failing clutch on the throttle vane control electric stepper motor. Lexus said an entire new throttle body is required as it is unserviceable. $2,500 for the part and $500 labor. Just because the wear item clutch was not reacting quickly enough to ECM commands. Did some digging and research and found the stepper motor is not called that in the parts supply chain worldwide. It is called a throttle control valve. Why because older tech cars use what is called an idle air control valve to bypass the throttle butterfly when idling, which can get coated in carbon and cause stumbling and poor off idle throttle response. Tons of videos online discussing how to clean them and avoid the stealership. Well this uses an electric motor with a clutch attached to a reduction gear set bolted to the side of the throttle body instead, there is no IAC valve. I wonder how many people ponied up for the 'dealer only service' instead of digging into the shop manual and finding what that Lexus calls an electric motor a valve and no searching parts on amazon or the local parts stores will show the electric motor you are looking for. Found lots of cheap Chinese copies once we knew what to look for and the dealer finally admitted they could put one in for $500 plus $750 for the additional labor of cleaning the throttle body and installing the stepper motor. Then on a hunch looked at the autozone website and found a Japanese made one with a great warranty and free shipping to our home. Plus they were running a 20% off discount for online orders over $150.
